title: Pulsed field ablation with Renal denervation for persistent Atrial fibrIllation: Rationale and design of the PRAISE-AF randomized trial.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia worldwide and is associated with increased risks of stroke, heart failure, hospitalization, disability, and mortality. Catheter ablation has become an established rhythm-control strategy for symptomatic AF; however, the recurrence rate after ablation remains substantial, especially in patients with persistent AF. Pulsed field ablation (PFA) is an emerging nonthermal ablation technology with myocardial tissue selectivity and a potentially improved safety profile compared with conventional thermal ablation. Renal denervation (RDN) reduces sympathetic nervous system activity and has shown promising effects in reducing AF recurrence when combined with catheter ablation, mainly in patients with paroxysmal AF and hypertension. Whether RDN combined with PFA improves rhythm outcomes in patients with persistent AF remains unknown.

TRIAL DESIGN: This is a single center, prospective, randomized, patient-blinded, sham-controlled pilot exploratory trial. A total of 86 patients with symptomatic persistent AF undergoing first-time catheter ablation will be enrolled and randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either PFA combined with RDN or PFA combined with a sham RDN procedure. Antiarrhythmic drugs (AADs) will be discontinued after the index procedure in both groups. The primary endpoint is freedom from documented atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence, including AF, atrial flutter, or atrial tachycardia lasting more than 30 seconds, within 12 months after a single ablation procedure without AADs. Secondary endpoints include freedom from atrial tachycardia recurrence within 3 months, AF burden, blood pressure changes, and major adverse cardiovascular events. Safety endpoints include cardiac, vascular, renal, and other procedure-related adverse events.

CONCLUSIONS: This trial will assess the safety and efficacy of PFA with RDN in a postablation contemporary persistent AF patient population.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov:NCT07320768.

title: Longitudinal Left Atrial Remodeling With Pharmacological Rhythm Versus Rate Control in Paroxysmal and Persistent Atrial Fibrillation.
summary:
PURPOSE: Evidence regarding left atrial (LA) remodeling with pharmacological rhythm control remains limited, particularly in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) outside heart-failure-specific populations.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 156 adults with paroxysmal or persistent AF receiving mutually exclusive pharmacological rate-control (n = 92) or rhythm-control (n = 64) therapy who underwent two transthoracic echocardiograms. LA remodeling was assessed using serial echocardiography, and clinical outcomes were evaluated after the second examination.

RESULTS: Among 74 patients with paired left atrial volume index (LAVI) measurements, LAVI increased from 39.9 to 50.3 mL/m2 with rate control (p < 0.001) but remained unchanged with rhythm control (44.9 to 43.4 mL/m2; p = 0.465). After adjustment for baseline LAVI and clinical covariates, rhythm control was associated with a 9.38 mL/m2 lower follow-up LAVI (95% CI, -15.53 to -3.24; p = 0.003). The association with lower follow-up LAVI was also observed among patients without heart failure and remained similar in sensitivity analyses. During post-landmark follow-up, rhythm control was associated with a lower hazard of all-cause mortality or stroke hospitalization (adjusted HR, 0.46; 95% CI, 0.24-0.88; p = 0.019).

CONCLUSION: Pharmacological rhythm control was associated with more favorable longitudinal LA remodeling than rate control, including among patients without heart failure, and was also associated with a lower hazard of subsequent all-cause mortality or stroke hospitalization.

title: Sleep-Disordered Breathing and Sleep Fragmentation in Relation to Atrial Fibrillation Risk: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is one of the most prevalent cardiac arrhythmias worldwide. This study aimed to evaluate the association between sleep-disordered breathing (SDB), primarily assessed using the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI), and AF risk, with additional analysis of sleep fragmentation parameters such as wake after sleep onset (WASO) and arousal index (AI).

METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis followed Cochrane Handbook recommendations and PRISMA guidelines, with protocol registration in PROSPERO (No. 127490). Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational cohort studies assessing sleep disturbances and AF were included. MEDLINE, Cochrane Library, and Scopus were searched from inception to February 2026. Extracted data included study characteristics, demographics, cardiovascular risk factors, and sleep metrics. Outcomes were incident and recurrent AF. A random-effects model was applied.

RESULTS: Twenty-one cohort studies (611,898 participants) were included. SDB was associated with increased incident AF risk (RR 1.67, 95% CI 1.41-1.97; I 2 = 66.5%), with consistent Bayesian estimates. A dose-response relationship showed a 2% increase in AF risk per unit rise in AHI. For AF recurrence, 11 studies (n = 1810) demonstrated a significant association (RR 1.55, 95% CI 1.40-1.72; I 2 = 0%), supported by Bayesian analysis.

CONCLUSION: Sleep disturbances are significantly associated with both incident and recurrent AF and may represent modifiable risk factors.

title: Development and Validation of a Novel Contact Force-Integrated Pulsed Field Quantization Index for Pulmonary Vein Isolation in a Porcine Model.
summary:
INTRODUCTION: There is no bipolar-specific quantitative ablation index currently available to guide pulsed field ablation (PFA). We aimed to develop and validate a novel contact force (CF)-integrated pulsed field quantization index (PFQI) for real-time lesion depth prediction during bipolar PFA.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In total, 27 healthy Yorkshire swine were included in a two-phase preclinical study. In Phase I, a nonlinear multivariable model was developed to derive a novel PFQI incorporating real-time CF, pulse train number, delivery voltage, and impedance variation. In Phase II, the PFQI was prospectively validated by comparing predicted with actual lesion depth, followed by PFQI-guided circumferential pulmonary vein isolation (PVI). Acute procedural success, 30-day PVI durability, and extracardiac safety were evaluated using serial electroanatomic mapping and blinded histopathological examination. Lesion depth was strongly associated with CF, pulse train number, voltage, and impedance change. The PFQI predicted actual depth with high accuracy (R = 0.94, R2 = 0.88; validation R2 = 0.82, slope = 1.014). In the validation cohort, 92% of predicted depths fell within ±0.75 mm of measured values. PFQI-guided PVI achieved 100% (6/6) acute isolation and 100% 30-day durable electrical isolation, with contiguous transmural fibrosis on histology. No collateral phrenic nerve, esophageal, or pulmonary vein injury occurred, and phrenic capture thresholds remained unchanged.

CONCLUSION: The PFQI is the first bipolar-specific, CF-integrated quantitative metric for PFA, enabling accurate, real-time lesion depth prediction. PFQI-guided PVI achieved consistent, durable, and safe PVI in a porcine model, providing a promising operator-independent quantitative strategy to optimize clinical bipolar PFA for atrial fibrillation.

title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure Versus Oral Anticoagulation for Prevention of Stroke or Systemic Embolism in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation: An Updated Meta-Analysis of 7004 Patients Across Six Randomized Trials.
summary:
INTRODUCTION: Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) is an emerging alternative for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) who are unsuitable for long-term oral anticoagulants (OACs). However, its efficacy and safety relative to OACs remain uncertain.

METHODS: Three databases were searched up to April 7, 2026, for randomized controlled trials comparing LAAC with OAC in patients with AF. Risk ratios with 95% confidence intervals were pooled using a random-effects model.

RESULTS: Six RCTs (n = 7004 patients) were analyzed. The risk of stroke or systemic embolism (SSE) did not differ significantly between the LAAC and OAC groups (RR: 1.10 [0.87-1.39]; p = 0.42). The risk of ischemic SSE was significantly increased with LAAC (RR: 1.41 [1.07-1.85]; p = 0.02) compared with OAC. No significant differences were observed in all-cause mortality (RR: 0.94 [0.81-1.09]), cardiovascular mortality (RR: 0.91 [0.69-1.21]), non-cardiovascular mortality (RR: 0.91 [0.75-1.12]), or hemorrhagic stroke (RR: 0.58 [0.29-1.17]). LAAC was associated with a similar risk of overall major bleeding (RR: 0.92 [0.77-1.09]) and low risk of non-procedural bleeding (RR: 0.61 [0.52-0.73]; p < 0.001) compared with OAC. Upon sensitivity analysis comparing LAAC with DOACs, the findings remained consistent across most clinical outcomes.

CONCLUSION: LAAC demonstrates comparable risks of SSE and major bleeding to OACs, but is associated with a higher risk of ischemic SSE and reduced non-procedural bleeding, supporting its use in selected patients at high risk for long-term bleeding while emphasizing individualized shared decision-making.

title: Changes in Lead Parameters of Cardiac Implantable Electronic Devices After VT/VF Ablation Using a Dual-Energy Lattice-Tip Catheter.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Interactions between cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) and pulsed field ablation (PFA) have been studied mainly in the context of atrial ablation, whereas the effects of ventricular ablation using a dual-energy lattice-tip catheter on ventricular leads remain unclear.

METHODS: This retrospective study involved 79 patients (mean age 60.9 ± 13.6 years) with an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator or cardiac resynchronization therapy defibrillator who underwent ventricular ablation using a lattice-tip catheter between February 2024 and November 2025. Pacing thresholds were assessed before, immediately after, and 3 months after ablation and standardized to a pulse width of 0.4 ms using the Lapicque-Weiss model. Marked acute threshold elevation was defined as an increase in pacing threshold of ≥ 1.0 V immediately after ablation. The anatomical relationship between ablation sites and ventricular lead locations was assessed based on the American Heart Association 17-segment model of the left ventricle and classified as corresponding when ablation involved the same or opposing ventricular region as the lead location, adjacent when ablation involved a directly adjacent region, and remote otherwise.

RESULTS: Marked acute pacing-threshold elevation occurred in 5 of 79 right ventricular (RV) leads (6.3%) and 2 of 22 evaluable left ventricular (LV) leads (9.1%). For RV leads, marked threshold elevation occurred in 4 of 14 patients (28.6%) in the corresponding group, 1 of 19 (5.3%) in the adjacent group, and none of 46 (0%) in the remote group. When threshold change was analyzed as a continuous variable, the acute increase was significantly greater in the corresponding group (+ 0.74 V; 95%CI 0.465-1.018) than in the adjacent (+ 0.31 V; 95%CI 0.076-0.550) and remote (+ 0.007 V; 95%CI - 0.145-0.160) groups. For LV leads, the pacing threshold increased significantly after ablation involving the corresponding segment (+ 0.71 V; 95%CI 0.167-1.245), although the overall association between anatomical relationship and threshold change was not significant. At 3 months, pacing thresholds in the corresponding groups were not significantly different from baseline for either RV or LV leads.

CONCLUSION: Marked acute pacing-threshold elevation was observed in both RV and LV leads after ventricular arrhythmia ablation using a dual-energy lattice-tip catheter. However, both RV and LV thresholds were no longer significantly different from baseline at 3 months. These findings suggest the importance of considering the anatomical relationship between ablation sites and CIED leads and of careful peri-procedural assessment of lead function during ventricular ablation.

title: Pulmonary Artery Approach for Radiofrequency Catheter Ablation of Atrial Tachycardia Originating From Left Atrial Post Wall: A Case Report.
summary:
INTRODUCTION: Due to limitations in ablation energy delivery and myocardial wall thickness, endocardial ablation of atrial tachycardia can sometimes be challenging.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In this case, ablation of the left atrial posterior wall shifted the earliest endocardial breakthrough site from the posterior wall to the roof, suggesting a potential epicardial origin near left atrial roof. The atrial arrhythmia was successfully eliminated via a right pulmonary artery approach.

CONCLUSION: The right pulmonary artery approach may be an effective strategy for ablating epicardial atrial arrhythmias, particularly those originating from the left atrial posterior roof.

title: Temporal Association Between Aromatase Inhibitor Initiation and New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation: A Case Report.
summary:
INTRODUCTION: Breast cancer is the most prevalent cancer among women worldwide with a higher probability of diagnosis in the postmenopausal years. Aromatase inhibitors (AIs) block the aromatase enzyme responsible for converting androgens into estrogens in the peripheral tissues, which become the main source for estrogen production in this population. Estrogen plays a key role in promoting vasodilation and inhibiting vascular injury and atherosclerosis development. Reduced levels can contribute to adipocyte hyperplasia, insulin resistance, and dyslipidemia, all of which are risk factors for atrial fibrillation.

PATIENT CASE: We describe the case of a 71-year-old postmenopausal female who presented to the emergency department with shortness of breath and was subsequently diagnosed with new-onset atrial fibrillation. This case report aims to evaluate whether there is a potential correlation between the initiation of an AI and the development of atrial arrhythmias.

DISCUSSION: While existing data suggest an association between AI use and atrial fibrillation, there lacks an elaborate understanding of the temporal relationship between the 2. This case highlights a potential association between AI therapy and unusually rapid-onset atrial fibrillation, demonstrating the need for further research and increased clinical awareness when managing patients receiving these treatments.

title: Blanking Period after Atrial Fibrillation Catheter Ablation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
summary: Background Atrial arrhythmias that recur within the first 3 months after atrial fibrillation (AF) catheter ablation are conventionally attributed to a "blanking period" and not classified as procedural failure. Accumulating evidence suggests that such early recurrences of atrial tachyarrhythmias (ERAT) may instead predict late recurrence, raising concern that the conventional 3-month window overestimates the duration during which recurrences are benign.Objective To assess the association between ERAT during each of the first 3 months after AF catheter ablation and late recurrence of atrial tachyarrhythmias (LRAT), and whether this association differs by ablation energy source.Methods We searched Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science without restriction on date or publication status for studies of AF catheter ablation reporting ERAT during defined intervals of the blanking period, stratified by subsequent LRAT status. Ablation energy sources included radiofrequency, cryoballoon, and pulsed field. The exposure was ERAT during the first, second, and third months after ablation, and the outcome was LRAT. Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models.Results Twelve studies comprising 7,751 patients (2,505 with LRAT, 5,246 without) were included. Mean follow-up was 22.0 months, mean age 60.7 years, 25.8% were women, 52.5% had paroxysmal AF, mean CHA2DS2-VASc score was 2.1, mean left atrial diameter 42.6 mm, and mean left ventricular ejection fraction 58.1%. ERAT was associated with subsequent LRAT, and the strength of this association increased across the blanking period: month 1 (12 studies; OR 1.76, 95% CI 1.01-3.08; p = 0.05), month 2 (10 studies; OR 3.46, 95% CI 2.15-5.57; p < 0.001), and month 3 (10 studies; OR 21.4, 95% CI 10.9-42.2; p < 0.001). The graded association was reproduced within the radiofrequency and cryoballoon subgroups.Conclusion ERAT was associated with subsequent LRAT throughout the blanking period, with a graded relationship that strengthened month by month and was strongest in the third month. These findings support a blanking period shorter than the conventional 3 months.

title: Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Atrial Fibrillation Recurrence After Catheter Ablation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Catheter ablation (CA) is an established rhythm-control strategy for atrial fibrillation (AF); however, AF recurrence remains common and is influenced by the underlying cardiometabolic substrate, including metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). This study aimed to evaluate the association of MASLD and MASLD-related fibrosis risk with AF recurrence following CA.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of observational studies reporting AF recurrence after CA, stratified by MASLD status and liver fibrosis risk, as assessed using the fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index and the non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) fibrosis score (NFS). Eligible studies included adults undergoing CA for AF with recurrence outcomes reported and stratified by MASLD or fibrosis risk categories.

RESULTS: A total of 160 records were identified, and seven studies were included in the qualitative synthesis. Six studies, including 2921 patients, contributed to the primary meta-analysis comparing MASLD versus no MASLD. An additional fibrosis-only study contributed to fibrosis-stratified analyses. The meta-analysis of six studies (MASLD: 894; non-MASLD: 2027) demonstrated that MASLD was associated with a significantly higher risk of AF recurrence after CA (risk ratio (RR) 1.77, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.43-2.18; p < 0.001; I2 = 64.1%). In a separate meta-analysis of five studies reporting adjusted estimates, MASLD remained significantly associated with recurrence (hazard ratio (HR) 2.13, 95% CI 1.49-3.04; p < 0.001; I2 = 70.5%). In fibrosis-stratified analyses, Intermediate/High FIB-4 (RR 2.03, 95% CI 1.27-3.26; p = 0.003; I2 = 71.3%) and Intermediate/High NFS (RR 1.65, 95% CI 1.12-2.43; p = 0.01; I2 = 49.9%) were associated with a higher risk of AF recurrence compared with low scores.

CONCLUSION: MASLD is associated with a significantly higher risk of AF recurrence after CA. Fibrosis risk stratification using FIB-4 and NFS also shows a significant association between Intermediate/High fibrosis and increased recurrence rates.

PROSPERO REGISTRATION: CRD420261335405, https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261335405.

title: Oral Anticoagulants in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation and Advanced or End-Stage Renal Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD) face a markedly elevated risk of both thromboembolic and bleeding events. While oral anticoagulation is the cornerstone of stroke prevention in AF, the optimal use of this treatment in patients with stage 4-5 CKD and end-stage renal disease (ESRD) undergoing dialysis remains uncertain, as these populations were largely excluded from the landmark trials that established the efficacy of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) in the general AF population. This study aimed to systematically evaluate and compare the efficacy and safety of vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) and DOACs, including factor Xa inhibitors, compared with alternative anticoagulation strategies or no anticoagulation in patients with AF and advanced CKD, including both non-dialysis-dependent stage 4-5 CKD and dialysis-dependent ESRD.

METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed (MEDLINE), the Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov was performed through January 30, 2026. Randomized controlled trials and observational cohort studies evaluating oral anticoagulation in adults with AF and stage 4-5 CKD (estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) <30 mL/min/1.73 m2, not on dialysis) or ESRD on dialysis were included. Outcomes of interest were a composite of stroke, transient ischemic attack or systemic embolism, major bleeding (International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis (ISTH) or study-defined), and all-cause mortality. Owing to clinical and methodological heterogeneity, evidence was synthesized narratively for most comparisons; randomized trials comparing factor Xa inhibitors with VKAs in dialysis-dependent patients were pooled in a random-effects meta-analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 20 studies met the inclusion criteria, comprising four randomized trials, one subgroup analysis of an RCT (ARISTOTLE), and fifteen observational cohorts. Four studies evaluated patients with advanced CKD not receiving dialysis, while sixteen focused on dialysis populations. In non-dialysis stage 4-5 CKD, DOAC therapy, particularly apixaban, was generally associated with comparable or reduced thromboembolic risk and lower rates of major bleeding compared with warfarin. Observational data also suggested a potential mortality benefit with DOACs compared with no anticoagulation. In contrast, findings in dialysis-dependent ESRD were heterogeneous. Warfarin was not consistently associated with reduced stroke risk compared with no anticoagulation and was frequently linked to elevated bleeding risk. Observational studies suggest that apixaban may confer a lower risk of major bleeding compared with VKAs while maintaining similar thromboembolic protection; however, randomized evidence has been limited and underpowered to demonstrate a definitive net clinical benefit. In a meta-analysis of the four dialysis randomized trials (n = 486), factor Xa inhibitors were associated with less ISTH major bleeding than VKAs (pooled risk ratio (RR) 0.64, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.42-0.99; not retained in Mantel-Haenszel or Hartung-Knapp sensitivity analyses), with no significant difference in stroke, transient ischemic attack or systemic embolism (pooled RR 0.46, 95% CI 0.20-1.02) or all-cause mortality (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.58-1.35).

CONCLUSION: The risk-benefit profile of oral anticoagulation differs across the CKD spectrum. In stage 4-5 CKD not requiring dialysis, DOACs appear to offer a more favorable safety profile than VKAs while preserving efficacy. In dialysis-dependent ESRD, the net clinical benefit of anticoagulation remains uncertain, particularly for warfarin. Further adequately powered randomized trials are needed to clarify optimal anticoagulation strategies in this high-risk population. Until then, treatment decisions should remain individualized, balancing thromboembolic and bleeding risk.

PROSPERO REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261286449.

title: Adverse Event Landscape of Pulsed Field Ablation Catheters: A Computational Review of FDA MAUDE Post-Market Surveillance Data.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) is Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-cleared for pulmonary vein isolation in atrial fibrillation. Using a keyword-based natural language processing pipeline applied to free-text narratives in the FDA MAUDE database, we aimed to characterize and compare adverse event and device malfunction profiles across the four cleared PFA systems.

METHODS: We retrieved 6930 MAUDE reports for FDA product code QZI (pulsed field ablation catheter) spanning December 13, 2023 through April 30, 2026, covering all four FDA-cleared PFA systems. Reports were deduplicated and assigned to a specific device system using manufacturer and brand name fields. Concatenated free-text narratives were classified into 11 predefined adverse event categories using multi-label keyword-based natural language processing. Device malfunction reports were additionally subclassified into one of 11 hardware-specific subtypes. Descriptive statistics were used throughout.

RESULTS: Of 6930 reports, 4185 (60.4%) were classified into at least one adverse event category. The three most common categories were device/catheter malfunction (2068; 29.8%), cardiac tamponade/pericardial effusion (915; 13.2%), and stroke/TIA/cerebral embolism (600; 8.7%). PFA-specific physiologic adverse events-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), hemolysis/acute kidney injury, and phrenic nerve palsy-accounted for 615 combined reports (8.9% of all reports). Fatality proportions were highest for vascular access complications (6.8%), esophageal/atrioesophageal injury (6.0%), and coronary artery spasm/STEMI (5.3%). Among malfunction reports, retraction/retrieval failure predominated for Farapulse (48.9%), while electrical/energy delivery failure was the leading subtype for PulseSelect (29.4%).

CONCLUSIONS: Natural language processing (NLP)-assisted keyword classification enables systematic, scalable characterization of adverse event patterns across nearly 7000 real-world PFA reports. PFA-specific physiologic adverse events are identifiable through post-market surveillance data and constitute a distinct safety phenotype separate from device malfunction. This approach provides a reproducible framework for near-real-time surveillance of novel cardiac ablation systems.

title: Fibroblast Activation Protein Inhibitor Positron Emission Tomography Imaging in Atrial Fibrillation: Current Evidence and Future Perspectives.
summary: Fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) has emerged as a promising molecular imaging modality for visualizing fibroblast activation and extracellular matrix remodeling. In addition to its established role in oncology imaging, FAPI PET/CT is gaining recognition in the evaluation of cardiovascular disease. Emerging evidence suggests that this technique may provide molecular insights into atrial fibroblast activation and the development of a fibrotic substrate in atrial fibrillation. Meanwhile, related findings from other arrhythmias further support a potential link between myocardial fibroblast activation and electrophysiological remodeling. This review summarizes the current evidence on FAPI PET/CT imaging in atrial fibrillation, discusses related findings in other cardiovascular conditions, and highlights future directions for research in arrhythmia imaging.

title: Risk of Atrial Fibrillation Recurrence After Modified Cox-Maze IV Surgery: Comparing Atrial Functional Mitral Regurgitation and Rheumatic Mitral Regurgitation.
summary:
BACKGROUND: The comparative efficacy of the modified Cox-Maze IV procedure (CMP IV) in treating atrial fibrillation (AF) in patients with atrial functional mitral regurgitation (AFMR) and those with rheumatic mitral regurgitation (RMR) remains inadequately characterized. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate and compare postoperative AF recurrence rates and clinical outcomes between these two etiologically distinct groups.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 221 patients (AFMR group: n = 53; RMR group: n = 168) with concomitant long-standing persistent AF who underwent mitral valve surgery combined with modified CMP IV or other concomitant procedures at our institution between January 2019 and September 2024. To address baseline imbalances, propensity score matching was performed at a 1:1 ratio, resulting in well-matched cohorts of 32 patients with AFMR and 32 with RMR patients for the final analysis. The primary endpoint was AF recurrence. Statistical comparisons utilized chi-square tests, t-tests, exact McNemar tests, and paired t-tests.

RESULTS: After PSM, 32 patients remained in each group with balanced baselines. The AFMR group showed a higher trend toward postoperative AF recurrence. Pre‑discharge AF recurrence rates did not differ significantly between groups (37.5% vs. 12.5%; p = 0.057), however, the risk of AF recurrence before discharge was significantly higher in the AFMR group (OR = 3.67, 95% CI: 1.02-13.14, p = 0.046). At the 1-year follow-up, a statistically significant difference in AF recurrence was observed between the two groups (31.2% vs 6.2%, p = 0.021), and the risk difference persisted (OR = 9.00, 95% CI: 1.14-71.04, p = 0.037). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed a significant difference in freedom from AF recurrence (log‑rank χ2 = 6.33; p = 0.012), supported by sensitivity analyses (log‑rank χ2 = 6.01; p = 0.014). Mortality did not differ at 30 days (3.1% vs. 0%; p = 1.000) or 1 year (3.1% vs. 3.1%; p = 1.000), with comparable overall survival (log‑rank p = 0.99).

CONCLUSIONS: In patients undergoing mitral valve surgery with modified CMP IV, those with AFMR exhibit a significantly higher risk of postoperative AF recurrence compared with patients with RMR, despite similar early-term survival outcomes. Postoperative AF monitoring should be intensified in patients with AFMR to improve long-term outcomes.

title: The "Floating Lotus" Sign on Intracardiac Echocardiography: Characterization and Predictors of a Novel Left Atrial Appendage Pseudo-Thrombus.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) is increasingly used for left atrial appendage (LAA) assessment during atrial fibrillation (AF) procedures. We describe a novel, thrombus-mimicking artifact on ICE, termed the "Floating Lotus" sign.

METHODS: In this retrospective multicenter study, we analyzed data from 172 patients undergoing ICE-guided AF ablation and/or LAA occlusion. The incidence, imaging features, and clinical correlates of the "Floating Lotus" sign were assessed.

RESULTS: The "Floating Lotus" sign was observed in 48 patients (27.9%). It manifested as a mobile, echogenic mass within an anechoic space, revealing an underlying pericardial effusion. Patients exhibiting the sign had a higher prevalence of recent stroke (35.4% vs. 15.3%, p = 0.004), heart failure (64.6% vs. 8.1%, p < 0.001), and larger left atrial diameter (44.3 ± 6.8 vs. 39.7 ± 5.4 mm, p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, only heart failure (left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) <55%) remained an independent predictor (odds ratio [OR] 14.39, 95% confidence interval [CI] 5.51-37.58, p < 0.001). Lower LAA emptying velocity was independently associated with persistent AF, higher CHA2DS2-VASc score, and recent stroke (all p < 0.05).

CONCLUSION: The "Floating Lotus" sign is a common ICE pseudo-thrombus, often associated with heart failure. Accurate recognition of this sign, based on its dynamic imaging features, is therefore critical to prevent misdiagnosis and avoid unnecessary procedural cancellation or anticoagulation changes.

title: Enhancer of Zeste Homolog 2 Inhibition Attenuates Atrial Fibrillation Post-Myocardial Infarction Through Reduced Atrial Fibrosis.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is one of the most prevalent arrhythmias following a myocardial infarction (MI), yet the pathogenesis associated with post-MI AF remains poorly understood. Enhancer of zeste homolog 2 (EZH2), an enzyme that regulates histone modifications, has been implicated in various cardiovascular diseases; however, the role of EZH2 in the development of post-MI AF also remains unclear.

METHODS: MI was induced in mice by ligation of the left anterior descending coronary artery (LAD), followed by intraperitoneal administration of GSK126 or vehicle control (polyethylene glycol 300 and saline).

RESULTS: MI significantly increased the incidence and duration of AF, while electrical mapping revealed decreased conduction velocity. These changes were accompanied by increased atrial fibrosis, which was associated with upregulation of EZH2 and trimethylated histone H3 at lysine 27 (H3K27me3). In GSK126-treated mice, the incidence of AF was reduced, along with a significant decrease in H3K27me3 expression and atrial fibrosis.

CONCLUSION: Upregulation of EZH2 is associated with post-MI AF. Pharmacological inhibition of EZH2 using GSK126 attenuates atrial fibrosis and reduces the incidence of AF. These findings suggest that EZH2 may represent a potential therapeutic candidate for post-MI AF, although further validation is required.

title: Clinical Impact of Interlesion Distance on Acute Pulmonary Vein Isolation Success in Patients With Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Achieving pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) through contiguous lesions is important for durable PVI treatment of atrial fibrillation (AF). We hypothesized that the flexible-tip TactiFlex catheter, with its enhanced stability, would allow for successful acute PVI even with an extended interlesion distance (ILD) of 6 mm.

METHODS AND RESULTS: The WILD (Wide ILD) PVI trial was a prospective, multicenter, single-blind randomized non-inferiority trial. A total of 94 patients with paroxysmal AF were enrolled and randomly allocated to either a wide ILD group (≤6 mm, n=52) or a standard ILD group (≤4 mm, n=42). The primary endpoint was acute PVI success, defined as first pass isolation without early reconnection. The non-inferiority margin was set at -10.0%. The 6-mm group did not meet the criteria for non-inferiority compared to the 4-mm group (56.7% vs. 68.7%; absolute difference: -11.9% [95% confidence interval: -25.7 to 1.8%]; P for non-inferiority=0.664). Conversely, the 6-mm strategy significantly reduced the total number of RF applications (47±10 vs. 73±17, P=0.001) and total ablation time (528±119 s vs. 825±233 s, P<0.001) compared to the 4-mm group.

CONCLUSIONS: The 6-mm ILD strategy was inferior to the standard 4-mm strategy for acute PVI success. Despite significant gains in procedural efficiency, maintaining an ILD ≤4 mm is recommended to ensure high acute procedural success when using the TactiFlex catheter.

title: Trends in the incidence of atrial fibrillation and the prescription of oral anticoagulants in adults with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease in UK primary care (2010-2022): a cohort study.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Understanding the burden of atrial fibrillation (AF) and oral anticoagulant (OAC) use in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is important for stroke prevention in this high-risk population. We assessed trends in AF incidence and OAC initiation among patients with COPD in UK primary care from 2010 to 2022.

METHODS: We assembled a cohort of all patients at least 50 years of age who contributed data to the UK Clinical Practice Research Datalink between January 1, 2010, and December 31, 2022, who had a physician diagnosis of COPD before or during the study period. Patients were followed-up until AF diagnosis, study end date (December 2022), death, or transfer out of practice. We estimated annual incidence rates of AF and subsequent OAC initiation using Poisson regression, stratified by age, sex, ethnicity, and COPD severity. We assessed predictors of AF and OAC initiation using Cox proportional hazards regression models.

FINDINGS: 444,668 patients with COPD were included (mean age 70 years, 51.8% male), contributing 2,284,799 person-years of follow-up. 37,645 (8.5%) patients were diagnosed with AF during the study period. The incidence of AF increased from 13.8 per 1000 person-years in 2010 to 19.3 in 2022 [rate ratio (RR) 1.29; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.07-1.56], and was higher in males, White individuals, those over 80 years, and patients with severe COPD. Only 23,094 patients (66.3%) were prescribed an OAC in the year following AF diagnosis, though OAC use increased 2.9-fold during this period (RR 2.91; 95% CI 2.33-3.65). OAC initiation remained lowest among patients aged 50-59 and ≥90 years, and non-White individuals. OAC use was also up to 25.0% (adjusted hazard ratio 0.75; 95% CI 0.69, 0.81) less prevalent among those with severe COPD.

INTERPRETATION: AF incidence and OAC initiation increased among patients with COPD in UK primary care over 2010-2022. However, OAC use remained suboptimal, especially among older patients, non-White individuals, and those with severe COPD. These potential treatment gaps highlight the need for further research on stroke prevention strategies in this high-risk population.

FUNDING: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial or not-for-profit sectors.

title: Arrhythmic risk in axial spondyloarthritis: a narrative review.
summary: Axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA) is a chronic systemic inflammatory disorder affecting the axial skeleton and potentially the peripheral joints as well as extraskeletal tissues. Chronic systemic inflammation is also known to play a major role in the pathogenesis of conduction disturbances and arrhythmias, through chronic fibrotic scarring and cytokine-mediated delay of atrioventricular (AV) conduction as well as atrial remodelling. More specifically, the prevalence of AV block appears to be high, resulting in an increased risk for pacemaker implantation. Furthermore, axSpA is associated with an increased prevalence of atrial fibrillation, even when adjusting for other cardiovascular risk predictors. As the development of arrhythmia in axSpA appears to be associated with disease activity, controlling the systemic inflammation could potentially offer a viable addition to conventional antiarrhythmic treatment. However, the possible proarrhythmic effects of conventional and newer anti-inflammatory drugs in patients with axSpA need to be further elucidated in the future.

title: Unintended right atrial lesions after monopolar biphasic lattice-tip pulsed-field ablation: a case series.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Monopolar biphasic pulsed-field ablation (PFA) delivered by a lattice-tip catheter may create deeper lesions than conventional bipolar systems. The impact on adjacent right atrial structures remains poorly characterized.

CASE SUMMARY: We report four patients undergoing pulmonary vein isolation using a lattice-tip PFA catheter. Post-procedural electroanatomic mapping revealed unintended right atrial lesions involving the posterior right atrium, interatrial septum, or superior vena cava. In patients with short anatomical distances between right pulmonary veins and adjacent right atrial structures, lesions developed despite apparently successful pulmonary vein isolation. Catheter instability related to coughing under deep sedation appeared to contribute to broader lesion formation in two cases.

DISCUSSION: These cases suggest that monopolar biphasic lattice-tip PFA may create unintended lesions in adjacent right atrial tissue when anatomical proximity is short or catheter stability is compromised. Awareness of these mechanisms may help optimize procedural safety and lesion delivery.

title: Discontinuation of oral anticoagulants is common after catheter ablation in older patients with atrial fibrillation.
summary:
AIMS: Guidelines recommend continuing oral anticoagulation (OAC) after atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation based on stroke risk, yet real-world post-procedural OAC management remains poorly characterized. We aimed to evaluate contemporary patterns of OAC use after AF ablation and identify predictors of OAC discontinuation.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Using Medicare claims from 2013-2022, we established a cohort of patients undergoing a first AF ablation and assessed patterns of OAC discontinuation during the subsequent year. We defined OAC discontinuation as a dispensing gap ≥60 days. Baseline characteristics were evaluated as predictors of discontinuation using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator Cox regression. Among 208 232 AF patients (mean age 74.5, 47% women) undergoing ablation, 58% were taking OAC following ablation, 24% discontinued between 3 and 12 months, 8% discontinued within 3 months, and 10% did not use OAC within 3 months. Apixaban was the most commonly used OAC agent, while the use of warfarin declined over time. The overall rate of repeated ablation was 26%. We found that 44% of patients with CHA2DS2-VASc score ≥3 discontinued OAC within 1 year after ablation. Higher CHA2DS2-VASc scores and longer pre-ablation OAC use were associated with lower discontinuation, whereas pre-ablation major bleeding, frailty, and use of warfarin (vs. direct OACs) increased the likelihood of discontinuation.

CONCLUSION: OAC discontinuation after AF ablation is common, including among patients at elevated stroke risk despite guideline recommendations for continued therapy. More data are needed on the clinical consequences of post-ablation OAC discontinuation.

title: Left Atrial Enlargement Identifies Risk of Stroke Independent of Atrial Fibrillation.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Left atrial (LA) enlargement has been proposed to increase stroke risk independent of atrial fibrillation (AF), but evidence accounting for AF over time is limited. We tested whether the association between LA enlargement and stroke persist independent of new-onset AF.

METHODS: In this observational study, participants from the Copenhagen General Population Study underwent cardiac computed tomography from 2010 through 2018 and were followed until December 2022. LA volume was indexed to body surface area. LA enlargement was defined using sex-specific cutoffs. The primary outcome was incident stroke. Secondary outcomes were incident AF, heart failure, dementia, and all-cause mortality. Individuals with baseline AF were excluded. Hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using cause-specific Cox models with AF modeled as a time-varying covariate.

RESULTS: Among 10 024 individuals (mean age 60 years, 57% women), 684 (6.8%) had LA enlargement. Over a median follow-up of 7.3 years stroke occurred in 356 individuals (3.6%). LA enlargement was associated with a higher absolute risk of stroke (11.1% versus 4.6%, risk difference 6.5% [95% CI, 2.4-10.6]) and an increased hazard (adjusted HR, 1.49 [95% CI, 1.09-2.05]; P=0.013), which remained similar after adjustment for incident AF, and in separate models using the CHA2DS2-VA score and P-wave terminal force in lead V1. LA enlargement was also associated with higher risk of AF (HR, 3.77 [95% CI, 3.00-4.73]) and heart failure (HR, 3.59 [95% CI, 2.54-5.06]) but not with dementia or all-cause mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: LA enlargement was associated with incident stroke independent of incident AF, supporting LA enlargement as a marker of thromboembolic risk.

title: Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing Improves Atrial Function and Reverses Atrial Remodeling in Dyssynchrony Heart Failure Model.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Left bundle branch area pacing may reduce new-onset atrial fibrillation. However, its mechanism and the comparison of atrial reverse remodeling effect between left bundle branch pacing (LBBP) and left ventricular septal pacing (LVSP) has not been elucidated. We aim to investigate reverse atrial remodeling by LBBP and LVSP in a canine model of rapid pacing-induced dyssynchronous heart failure (DHF).

METHODS: Twenty-six beagles followed a 6-week protocol: controls (n=4), rapid atrial pacing (n=4), DHF (n=6), DHF+LBBP and DHF+LVSP (3 weeks DHF followed by 3 weeks LBBP or LVSP, both n=6). Atrial emptying fraction, functional, and electrophysiological parameters were dynamically assessed. Atrial fibrosis was analyzed in tissue samples.

RESULTS: Within 3 weeks DHF increased atrial volumes and diminished RA and LA emptying fraction and strains significantly compared with baseline. Subsequent 3 weeks of LBBP increased emptying fraction and strains significantly. At week 6, P-wave duration was shorter in DHF+LBBP than in DHF. Atrial fibrillation was only inducible in DHF animals. Left atrial appendage levels of collagen I/III and α-SMA deposition and fibrosis were lower in DHF+LBBP compared with DHF animals. LBBP reversed atrial structural and electrical parameters to the levels in rapid atrial pacing animals. LVSP improved those parameters compared with those in DHF but did not normalize them to the levels in the rapid atrial pacing animals.

CONCLUSIONS: LBBP significantly reverses DHF-induced functional, cellular, and molecular remodeling in the atria, while a smaller amelioration is achieved with LVSP. The findings may explain the reduction in new-onset atrial fibrillation after LBBP.

title: First-in-human experience and one-year outcomes using a novel conformal pulsed-field ablation balloon catheter for pulmonary vein isolation in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Thermal balloon catheters have improved the efficiency of pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) in atrial fibrillation (AF). Reports assessing additional safety and effectiveness of pulsed field ablation (PFA) balloon catheters for PVI are limited. This study aims to assess the safety and effectiveness of a conformal PFA balloon catheter for PVI in paroxysmal AF.

METHODS: 35 patients with paroxysmal AF (PAF) were treated with a PFBalloon catheter (Biphasic, Bipolar, 750 V). The balloon was inflated with 10:1 saline/contrast, with volume adjusted for spherical wide-antral or pear-shaped ostial-junction PV ablation to ensure optimal tissue contact. The primary safety endpoint was absence of periprocedural primary adverse events. The primary effectiveness endpoint was acute PVI. The secondary effectiveness endpoint included durable PVI assessed by remapping at three months post-ablation and 1-year clinical outcomes.

RESULTS: All targeted PVs (142/142) in 35 patients were acutely isolated, with 32.3 ± 4.5 applications per patient and 7.9 ± 1.0 per vein. Procedure and left atrial dwell times were 133 ± 46 and 56 ± 25 min, respectively. No hemolysis-related acute kidney injury or severe device-related complications occurred. PVI durability was 76.0% (19/25) per patient and 93.1% (95/102) per vein. After a median follow-up of 367 (interquartile range 357-380) days, 1-year Kaplan-Meier estimate for freedom from atrial arrhythmia (AF/atrial flutter/atrial tachycardia) ≥30 s was 90.7% (95% CI, 81.2%-100%).

CONCLUSIONS: The conformal PFBalloon catheter demonstrated favorable safety, efficiency, and effectiveness for PVI in PAF patients, achieving durable lesions and a high rate of freedom from atrial arrhythmias recurrence.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: clinicaltrials.gov NCT07320976.

title: Cardiometabolic health-frailty phenotypes and bidirectional transitions between atrial fibrillation and heart failure: multistate trajectories and proteomic signatures.
summary:
OBJECTIVE: To examine whether a joint cardiometabolic health-frailty phenotype is associated with incident atrial fibrillation (AF), incident heart failure (HF) and progression to AF-HF comorbidity, and to identify candidate circulating protein signals related to this phenotype.

METHODS: Among 319,048 UK Biobank participants without AF or HF, cardiometabolic status (healthy [CMH] or unhealthy [CMU]) and Frailty status (non-frail [NF] or pre-frail/frail [F]) defined four phenotypes. Cox and clock-forward multistate models estimated disease-specific and transition-specific hazards. Proteomic feature selection and exploratory mediation analyses included 28,206 participants with Olink plasma proteomic data.

RESULTS: During follow-up, 17,844 participants developed AF, 5,410 developed HF, and 2,403 and 791 progressed from AF and HF, respectively, to comorbidity. Compared with CMH-NF, CMU-F was associated with the greatest risks of incident HF (hazard ratio (HR), 2.76; 95% confidence interval (CI), 2.59-2.95) and AF (HR, 1.49; 95% CI, 1.43-1.55). Corresponding multistate HRs were 2.98 (95% CI, 2.76-3.22) for baseline-to-HF, 1.45 (1.39-1.51) for baseline-to-AF, 1.76 (1.57-1.98) for AF-to-comorbidity, and 1.27 (1.02-1.57) for HF-to-comorbidity. Positive additive interactions indicated excess risk from coexisting cardiometabolic unhealthiness and frailty. Thirteen proteins showed statistical mediation signals for both outcomes; FABP4 yielded the largest positive mediated proportions (AF, 49.8%; HF, 32.9%) and transition-specific signals for baseline-to-AF and AF-to-comorbidity.

CONCLUSIONS: Coexisting cardiometabolic unhealthiness and frailty identified individuals at greatest risk of AF, HF, and subsequent comorbidity. Exploratory proteomic analyses identified FABP4 as the most consistent preliminary signal, which warrants further validation in independent cohorts.

title: C-Reactive Protein as a Predictor of Cardiovascular Events and Mortality in Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Propensity-Matched Analysis Using the TriNetX Research Network.
summary:
INTRODUCTION: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) increases cardiovascular disease risk through systemic inflammation, particularly through elevated C-reactive protein (CRP). This study investigated whether CRP stratification predicts mortality and cardiovascular events in OSA patients.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort analysis using the TriNetX Research Network, encompassing electronic health records from 130 healthcare institutions. Adults (ages 18-90 years) with OSA were stratified by CRP concentration: elevated (≥ 3.0 mg/L) versus low (≤ 2.9 mg/L). After propensity score matching for demographics and comorbidities, 240,727 participants per cohort were followed for five years. Primary outcome was all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes included cardiovascular events, arrhythmias, and acute kidney injury.

RESULTS: Elevated CRP was associated with significantly higher all-cause mortality (11.3% versus 7.0%; HR 1.695, 95% CI 1.662-1.727; p < 0.001). The elevated CRP group demonstrated heightened cardiovascular risk: cardiogenic shock (1.0% versus 0.5%; HR 2.003), heart failure (9.8% versus 6.5%; HR 1.594), pulmonary hypertension (4.9% versus 3.4%; HR 1.508), and acute kidney injury (11.0% versus 6.4%; HR 1.825), all p < 0.001. Arrhythmic complications were also increased: atrial fibrillation/flutter (6.3% versus 4.8%; HR 1.372) and ventricular tachycardia (2.3% versus 1.8%; HR 1.388), both p < 0.001.

CONCLUSION: Elevated CRP constitutes a robust predictor of mortality and cardiovascular morbidity in OSA populations. Assessment of inflammatory biomarkers may enhance risk stratification, informing intensified monitoring and targeted therapeutic interventions.

title: Fibrosis burden and spatial pattern affect left atrial appendage stasis in multi-beat multi-physics simulations.
summary: Purpose: Atrial fibrosis is associated with thromboembolic risk in atrial fibrillation, but it remains unclear how fibrosis-related contractile impairment alters blood transport in the left atrium (LA) and left atrial appendage (LAA). Prior multi-physics simulations coupling electromechanical (EM) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models showed that fibrosis impairs LA function and flow, but were limited to booster-only contraction and could not separate the effects of fibrosis burden from its spatial distribution. Here, we examined how fibrosis burden and spatial pattern independently relate to long-term LA and LAA hemodynamics in full-cycle, multi-beat simulations on a common LA anatomy. Methods: Three fibrosis patterns derived from late gadolinium enhancement MRI were applied globally to a common LA anatomy at matched burdens of 15.6% and 31.2%, yielding six global-fibrosis cases and a non-fibrotic reference. Two patterns were also confined to the LAA at local burdens of 10%, 25%, and 50%, yielding six LAA-fibrosis cases. A 3D EM model of the LA anatomy coupled to a 0D circulatory model resolved the reservoir, conduit, and booster phases, and the EM-derived wall motion drove subsequent multi-beat CFD simulations. Region-specific emptying fraction (EF), non-dimensional kinetic energy (KE), and the 90th percentile of blood residence time (T R ) were evaluated in the LA and LAA. Results: Left ventricular stroke volume remained nearly constant across cases, whereas increasing global fibrosis burden progressively reduced LA and LAA EF (LA: 36% to 30-31%; LAA: 44% to 28-38%), lowered both active and passive LA EF, and monotonically increased LA T R across all patterns. Non-dimensional LA KE showed an approximately quadratic association with LA EF across patterns, whereas LAA KE was more scattered but still increased with LAA EF. In contrast, the 90th percentile of LAA T R did not increase monotonically with decreasing LAA EF for one pattern. When fibrosis was confined to the LAA, non-dimensional LAA KE collapsed onto a single relationship with LAA EF for both patterns, whereas LAA T R followed distinct, non-monotonic trends. Conclusions : Fibrosis burden, through its association with functional impairment, predominantly governed whole-LA hemodynamics, whereas LAA stasis additionally depended on the spatial distribution of fibrosis. In the LAA-fibrosis cases, LAA EF was a robust descriptor of chamber-averaged KE regardless of fibrosis pattern, but did not fully explain LAA residence time. These findings support evaluating imaging-derived fibrosis pattern, in addition to fibrosis burden and functional metrics, as a potential determinant of LAA transport and stasis. Its incremental value for thrombogenic-risk assessment requires prospective clinical validation.

title: Reliability and accuracy of medication-based performance measures for assessment of outpatient cardiology clinicians.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Multiple performance measures are used to assess the management of common cardiovascular conditions, such as coronary artery disease (CAD), heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), and atrial fibrillation (AF). These measures are sometimes used to assess individual clinicians, despite lack of evidence of reliability and accuracy. We used national Veteran Affairs (VA) data to test medication-based performance measures for assessment of clinician performance in outpatient cardiology care.

METHODS: This retrospective study examined VA cardiology clinician/Veteran dyads from 2017-2023 to evaluate 10 medication-based performance measures for CAD, HFrEF, or AF with elevated stroke risk. Achievement of each performance measure was defined as an active prescription of an indicated medication for each eligible patient encounter, summarized at the clinician level. Reliability was calculated using the beta-binomial method. A Bayesian causal model was used to assess the impact of case complexity on performance measure achievement. Finally, we performed peer review of a subset of cases (n = 952) to assess the accuracy of three representative performance measures.

RESULTS: Of 456,071 unique cardiology encounters included in this study, 312,331 included CAD, 224,599 included HFrEF, and 178,678 included AF. These patients were treated by 1,043 cardiology clinicians. Median performance measure achievement ranged from 0.23 (SGLT2i for HFrEF) to 0.99 (beta blocker for HFrEF). Measure reliability varied from 0.63 to 0.90. Case complexity did not significantly affect performance measure achievement. Using peer review as the gold standard, accuracy was poor to moderate (balanced accuracy 0.51-0.73), and measures underestimated performance relative to peer review.

CONCLUSIONS: Ten medication-based performance measures for CAD, HFrEF, and AF can be efficiently measured using electronic health record data, and most have sufficient reliability to support clinician benchmarking and the identification of potential care gaps without need for risk adjustment. However, suboptimal accuracy compared with a peer review gold standard indicates that these measures may be insufficient as a standalone assessment of clinician quality.

title: Electrical Alternans With Alternating Left Ventricular Apical Ballooning Mimicking Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy in a Patient With Extreme QT Prolongation.
summary:
INTRODUCTION: We report unique and rare findings of coupled electrical and mechanical alternans in a patient with extreme QT prolongation.

METHODS: A 5-year-old girl with congenital long QT syndrome type 3 developed alternate left ventricular apical ballooning precipitated by mycoplasma pneumonia and azithromycin exposure.

RESULTS: During atrial pacing, electrocardiography showed beat-to-beat alternation not only in T-wave morphology but also in QRS configuration, ST segment, and QT interval. These electrical changes were tightly associated with mechanical alternans: beats with markedly prolonged QT intervals showed normal left ventricular (LV) contraction, whereas beats with shorter QT intervals and ST elevation exhibited LV apical ballooning. Treatment with mexiletine shortened the QT interval, abolished both electrical and mechanical alternans, and restored normal LV function.

CONCLUSIONS: Alternate LV apical ballooning mimicking Takosubo cardiomyopathy can be seen in a patient with extreme QT prolongation. These findings probably reflected a functional intraventricular conduction block due to marked spatial heterogeneity of repolarization between the LV base and apex.

title: Cardiac segmentation for ventricular tachycardia radioablation and radiotherapy patients with cardiac implants.
summary: Deep-learning (DL) segmentation enables cardiac substructure (CS) delineation for advanced cardiac-sparing radiation therapy (RT). Patients presenting for RT may have implantable devices (cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs)) and metal artifacts. Stereotactic body RT (SBRT) is used to treat ventricular tachycardia (VT), a population frequently with ICDs. We apply a DL model for RT patients with ICDs or undergoing VT-SBRT, enabling segmentation and CS-level dose analysis. CT simulation (CT-SIM) of 19 patients with ICDs and received VT-SBRT were evaluated. A validated segmentation model was retrained using a highly-curated CT-SIM cohort, supplemented with ICD images for training and validation, with a hold-out ICD test set (n=10), to predict 20 CS. Additional CT-SIM datasets included cancer-RT patients with (n=9) and without (n=10) ICDs to evaluate generalizability. The retrained ICD-supplemented model was compared against a non-ICD model using Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), 95% Hausdorff distance (HD95), and Wilcoxon signed-rank test (p<0.05). Dosimetric evaluation was performed for VT-SBRT CS. For VT-SBRT, the ICD-supplemented model achieved average DSC/HD95 of 0.71(0.19)/10.7(22.5)mm respectively, outperforming (p<0.05) the non-ICD model. On CT-SIM with ICDs, average DSC/HD95 were 0.70(0.22)/7.9(5.1)mm respectively, outperforming (p<0.05) the non-ICD model. On CT-SIM without ICDs, the average DSC was 0.74(0.17) (Non-ICD, DSC, 0.75(0.16), p<0.05) and average HD95 was 5.5(3.1)mm (Non-ICD, HD95, 5.3(2.8mm)). For VT-SBRT, CS dose depended on target location, with higher relative dose delivered to the ventricles, tricuspid valve, atrioventricular node, and left coronary arteries than other CS. ICD-supplemented training improved CS segmentation despite metal artifacts without meaningfully degrading non-ICD performance, supporting segmentation and CS-level dosimetry in ICD populations.

title: Rising Obesity-Driven Cardiac Mortality Among Young Adults in the United States: A 25-Year Retrospective Analysis (1999-2023).
summary:
BACKGROUND: Obesity is a growing risk factor for cardiovascular disease and mortality in the United States, particularly among younger adults.

METHODS: Using the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Wide-Ranging Online Data for Epidemiologic Research Multiple Cause of Death database, we retrospectively analyzed trends and disparities in obesity-related cardiac mortality among US individuals aged 15 to 44 years from 1999 to 2023, stratified by sex, race, urbanization, and census region. Deaths were identified using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) codes for obesity and cardiac conditions, including ischemic heart disease, sudden cardiac death, arrhythmias, and heart failure. Age-adjusted mortality rates were calculated using joinpoint regression and expressed as annual percentage change with 95% CIs.

RESULTS: Between 1999 and 2023, 51 860 obesity-related cardiac deaths were recorded. The age-adjusted mortality rates increased from 0.9 (95% CI, 0.8-0.9) to 2.5 (95% CI, 2.4-2.6) per 100 000. Mortality was highest during the COVID-19 pandemic (2019-2021). Men consistently had higher age-adjusted mortality rates than women. Black or African American and American Indian/Alaska Native individuals showed the highest racial disparities. The South and nonmetropolitan areas had the highest regional mortality, with Alaska recording the highest state-level age-adjusted mortality rate in 2023 (6.0 per 100 000). Mortality largely returned to baseline across most groups from 2021 to 2023.

CONCLUSIONS: Obesity-related cardiac mortality has risen in the United States over the past 2 decades with notable disparities across sex, race, region, and urbanization. These findings underscore the need for targeted public health interventions in high-risk populations to reduce premature cardiovascular deaths and reverse this trend.

title: Twenty years in the battle against sudden cardiac death: progress, pitfalls, and prospects for the future.
summary: Sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) is a life-threatening emergency that requires immediate intervention from lay responders. To address this critical need, the national Sudden Cardiac Arrest Foundation (SCAF) was established in 2005 to raise awareness, promote community engagement, and support survivors. The history of cardiopulmonary resuscitation, defibrillation, and public response programs illustrates decades of progress in resuscitation science and has helped lay the groundwork for the creation of SCAF. In addition to serving as a trusted information hub, SCAF leads several key initiatives. The Cardiac Arrest Survivor Alliance™ provides an online community for those affected by cardiac arrest, offering connection, support, and resources. The Call-Push-Shock campaign promotes three lifesaving steps to address out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: call 911, perform CPR, and use an automated external defibrillator (AED). While SCA remains a major cause of death, significant progress has been made in public education and response. Technological innovations such as dispatcher-assisted CPR, the widespread placement of AEDs, and improved EMS and cardiac arrest registries, have all strengthened the chain of survival. Public understanding has also improved, with the media increasingly distinguishing SCA from heart attacks, thanks in part to SCAF's tireless advocacy. As SCAF marks its 20th anniversary, the organization celebrates two decades of progress and looks ahead with optimism. Its mission remains steadfast: to raise awareness, empower bystanders to act, support survivors, and advance innovations that reduce preventable deaths from sudden cardiac arrest.

title: Intraoperative Application of the PRAETORIAN Score to Predict Optimal Subcutaneous Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillator Placement
summary: Background The PRAETORIAN score (PS) estimates the risk of defibrillation failure after subcutaneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (S-ICD) implantation based on postoperative chest radiography in the standing position. However, the usefulness of assessing the PS in the supine position intraoperatively has not yet been established.Methods We evaluated conventional (standing) and intraoperative supine PS in 124 consecutive Japanese patients undergoing S-ICD implantation. Changes between conventional and supine PS values were analyzed in two ways: (1) the presence of any difference in the absolute PS values regardless of the risk category, and (2) changes in clinically relevant risk categories for conversion failure (low, intermediate, or high risk). Predictors of discordance between the two assessments were also investigated.Results The median conventional PS was 30; 116 and 8 patients were classified as having low and intermediate risk of conversion failure, respectively. Numerical differences between the conventional and supine PS values were observed in 13 patients. However, clinically meaningful risk reclassification occurred in only two patients, suggesting that intraoperative supine PS assessment may underestimate PRAETORIAN score-based risk classification in a small subset of patients. Among patients with numerical PS changes, supine PS was significantly lower than conventional PS. An elevated BMI was strongly associated with PS discordance. Exploratory receiver operating characteristic curve analysis identified a BMI cutoff of 25.6 kg/m2 for discriminating patients with numerical PS discordance.Conclusions Intraoperative supine PS assessment shows excellent concordance with conventional standing PS and may provide a practical tool for confirming appropriate system positioning in most Japanese patients.

title: Successful Bailout Retrieval of an Active-Fixation Atrial Leadless Pacemaker Following Suspected Tissue Entrapment During Repositioning
summary: An 81-year-old woman with a medical history of mechanical mitral valve replacement, Maze procedure, and multiple myeloma presented with symptomatic sinus arrest and underwent AVEIR DR implantation. Although the AVEIR VR was successfully implanted, optimal electrical parameters could not be achieved during AVEIR AR placement. During repositioning of the AVEIR AR, myocardial entrapment with helix stretching was encountered. Here, we report that advancing the protective sleeve to fully encapsulate the device potentially enabled safe and successful retrieval.

title: Cardiac resynchronization therapy outcomes by sex and QRS duration: insights from AdaptResponse and a Real-world registry.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Sex-related differences in cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) outcomes in heart failure (HF) patients, particularly at shorter QRS durations, remain incompletely defined. We evaluated outcomes by sex and QRS duration in AdaptResponse trial and, pooled with Medtronic product surveillance registry (PSR) data, evaluated mortality comparing CRT and no CRT.

METHODS AND RESULTS: AdaptResponse patients (symptomatic HF, LVEF≤35%, Strauss-LBBB, and normal atrioventricular conduction; 43% women) were analyzed by sex and baseline QRS (150ms cut-off), and pooled with PSR CRT and No CRT groups meeting CRT indications. Average treatment effect on treated (ATT) propensity weighting was used to standardize the PSR groups to AdaptResponse baseline characteristics. All-cause mortality was compared between the pooled CRT patients and No CRT controls with weighted Cox models. In AdaptResponse, adjusted mortality rates did not differ significantly between women and men (HR 0.91, 95% CI: 0.72-1.15; p=0.45), and no interaction was observed between sex and QRS (p=0.31). Adjusted mortality in women with QRS<150ms was not statistically different from men with QRS≥150ms (HR 1.02, CI: 0.75-1.38). After ATT-weighting and adjustment, CRT was observed to be associated with lower mortality versus No CRT across sex and QRS subgroups (QRS 120-149ms: HR 0.50, CI: 0.31-0.82 for women and HR 0.51, CI: 0.31-0.86 for men; QRS≥150ms: HR 0.46, CI: 0.28-0.74 for women and HR 0.46, CI: 0.29-0.72 for men; all p<0.05).

CONCLUSION: In this exploratory analysis, among patients with QRS 120-149ms, CRT was associated with a 49% and 50% relative mortality reduction in men and women, respectively, through five years of follow-up compared to No CRT controls. In AdaptResponse, mortality in women with these shorter QRS durations was similar to men with QRS≥150ms. These observational findings are hypothesis-generating and suggest a potential benefit of CRT in this patient population, particularly for women, but have not been confirmed in a randomized trial.

title: Procedural Outcomes of Leadless Pacemaker Extraction and Retrieval: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis With Descriptive Synthesis of Post-Implant Management.
summary:
INTRODUCTION: Leadless pacemakers reduce lead- and pocket-related complications, but pooled evidence on the procedural outcomes of their extraction and retrieval remains limited.

METHODS AND RESULTS: A systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO CRD420261397097) evaluated leadless pacemaker extraction or retrieval. The primary analysis pooled independent full-text studies reporting at least three attempted removals using a random-effects binomial-normal generalized linear mixed model. Outcomes were procedural success and major retrieval-related procedural events. Eight studies contributed 303 removal attempts to the primary success analysis, and six studies contributed 293 subjects or procedures to the safety analysis. Pooled procedural success was 89.1% (95% CI, 85.1% to 92.2%), and major retrieval-related procedural events occurred in 3.8% (95% CI, 2.1% to 6.7%); between-study heterogeneity was not detected for either outcome. Sensitivity estimates for major events ranged from 3.3% to 4.1%. Reported dwell time before removal ranged from intraprocedural retrieval to 9 years. A secondary descriptive synthesis of 96 clinical publications and five cohorts with complete denominators characterized post-implant management without cross-study pooling.

CONCLUSION: Leadless pacemaker removal was successful in approximately nine of 10 attempts, while qualifying major retrieval-related events occurred in approximately four of 100 safety denominators. The certainty of evidence was very low. Post-implant management patterns varied across cohorts and could not be pooled.

title: Development and Clinical Evaluation of a Vascular Access-Optimized Perioperative Care Pathway for Temporary Pacemaker Implantation.
summary:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate the safety and feasibility of a perioperative care pathway for temporary pacemaker implantation using a median cubital vein approach.

METHODS: A total of 238 patients who underwent non-emergency temporary pacemaker implantation between September 2020 and October 2024 were enrolled and randomly assigned to either the femoral vein group (F group) or the median cubital vein group (M group). The M group received a standardized perioperative nursing care pathway tailored to median cubital vein access. Electrode dislodgement and procedure-related complications were compared between the groups. Patient comfort and emotional status were assessed using the General Comfort Questionnaire (GCQ), the Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS), and the Self-Rating Depression Scale (SDS). The quality of nursing care was evaluated using predefined quality control standards.

RESULTS: The M group demonstrated significantly lower rates of electrode dislodgement and complications than the F group (p < 0.05). Postoperatively, GCQ scores were significantly higher in the M group, whereas SAS and SDS scores were significantly lower (all p < 0.05). Compliance with nursing care quality standards was also higher in the M group (p < 0.01). Within-group analysis showed significant reductions in SAS and SDS scores in both groups before pacemaker removal, with greater improvements observed in the M group (p < 0.05). No significant improvement in GCQ scores was observed in the F group. The M group showed also higher adherence to the standardized perioperative nursing care pathway than the F group (p < 0.01).

CONCLUSION: Compared with femoral vein access, temporary pacemaker implantation via the median cubital vein was associated with improved safety, greater patient comfort, and better emotional outcomes. The vascular access-optimized perioperative care pathway provided meaningful clinical benefits and warrants broader implementation.

title: Rapid Radiological Disappearance of Pancreatic Duct Stones Following Oral Trimethadione.
summary: A 59-year-old man with chronic pancreatitis, surgically altered anatomy, and an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator presented with acute exacerbation caused by cast-like obstructive pancreatic duct stones. Endoscopic therapy was considered technically difficult, and extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy was avoided. While delayed surgical drainage was being considered, off-label oral trimethadione was started after institutional ethics approval. Computed tomography 2 weeks later showed disappearance of the stones and improvement of ductal dilatation. No adverse events occurred, and surgery was deferred. This case suggests that trimethadione may be a potential salvage option when standard interventions are infeasible.

title: Breast cancer metastasis mimicking pacemaker pocket infection: a diagnostic pitfall and long-term preservation of the cardiac implantable electronic device-a case report.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) pocket infection is the most common infectious complication following pacemaker implantation or generator replacement and generally requires complete device and lead extraction according to current international guidelines. Nevertheless, non-infectious disorders, including malignant disease, may closely mimic pocket infection, creating a challenging differential diagnosis and potentially leading to delayed diagnosis or unnecessary CIED extraction. Neoplastic involvement of the CIED pocket is exceptionally rare.

CASE SUMMARY: An 81-year-old woman with a permanent VDD pacemaker implanted for symptomatic complete atrioventricular block underwent elective generator replacement in January 2020. Several months later, she developed progressive pain, erythema, and swelling over the left prepectoral generator pocket, raising suspicion of CIED pocket infection. Despite empirical antibiotic therapy and surgical pocket revision, repeated microbiological cultures remained sterile and no intraoperative evidence of infection was identified. Progressive enlargement of the lesion prompted further diagnostic investigation. Ultrasonography demonstrated a highly vascularized solid mass, while contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) revealed a lobulated soft-tissue lesion adjacent to the pacemaker generator together with bilateral pulmonary nodules, bilateral breast nodules, and multiple osteolytic skeletal lesions. Complete surgical excision of the pocket mass was performed while preserving the pacing system. Histopathological examination demonstrated metastatic well-differentiated invasive ductal carcinoma of breast origin (oestrogen receptor 95%, progesterone receptor 95%, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 score 0, Ki-67 7%). The unusually large pocket lesion represented the first clinical manifestation leading to the diagnosis of an otherwise clinically occult disseminated breast carcinoma. Following oncological staging, endocrine therapy consisting of letrozole followed by the addition of a CDK4/6 inhibitor resulted in prolonged disease control. At the most recent follow-up in 2026, contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated partial regression of metastatic disease, without local recurrence, while the CIED continued to function normally.

DISCUSSION: Persistent or atypical CIED pocket lesions associated with negative microbiological investigations should prompt consideration of alternative diagnoses, including foreign-body reaction. Integration of clinical assessment, microbiology, multimodality imaging, and histopathological examination may prevent unnecessary device extraction, facilitate timely oncological diagnosis, and allow successful long-term preservation of a normally functioning CIED.

title: Appropriate ICD Therapies in Primary Prevention: A Propensity-Matched Comparison of Contemporary and Historic Heart Failure Cohorts.
summary:
BACKGROUND: In heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), a substantial proportion of deaths are arrhythmic. Implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs) are recommended for primary prevention in patients with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≤ 35% despite guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT), but landmark trials predate widespread use of angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors (ARNI) and sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i), raising uncertainty about arrhythmic risk in the contemporary treatment era.

METHODS: We retrospectively studied consecutive HFrEF patients undergoing primary-prevention ICD implantation at a single center (2015-2022), categorized into historical-era and contemporary-era cohorts by ARNI/SGLT2i adoption. Propensity-score matching balanced baseline characteristics. The primary endpoint was time to first appropriate ICD therapy (antitachycardia pacing or shock).

RESULTS: Of 289 patients (mean age 62 ± 11 years, 82% male), 234 (117 per group) remained after matching. Mean follow-up was 51 months. Appropriate ICD therapy incidence did not differ significantly between contemporary-era and historical-era cohorts (hazard ratio [HR] 1.52, 95% CI 0.84-2.72; p = 0.165). Competing-risk-adjusted cumulative incidence was numerically higher in the contemporary-era cohort at a pre-specified 36-months horizon, consistent with a sensitivity analysis using an expanded propensity-score model (HR 1.55, 95% CI 0.82-2.94).

CONCLUSION: ICD therapy rates were not significantly different between the contemporary-era and historical-era cohorts, a finding robust to sensitivity and competing-risk analyses. These results should be interpreted cautiously, as the study may be underpowered to detect modest differences, and clinically relevant effects cannot be excluded.
